subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: It is given that Rolle's theorem holds for the function f(x) = x³ + bx² + ax on [1, 3] with c = 2 + 1/√3. Find the values of a and b.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say which two conditions Rolle's theorem gives, and what you do with the given c.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Use f(1) = f(3)
steps.margin_note: First mark. The question SAYS Rolle's theorem holds, so its condition f(1) = f(3) may be used as a given fact — you are not asked to prove it. That equation alone links a and b.
steps.memory_tip: Rolle's theorem has two parts: equal end values, and a zero derivative inside. Two parts, two unknowns.
lines: Rolle's theorem holds here, so f(1) = f(3) and f′(c) = 0

recall.must_convey: That Rolle's theorem gives f(1) = f(3), and that this equation reduces to a + 4b = −13.
accept: the end values are equal so f of one equals f of three
put f one equal to f three and get a plus four b equals minus thirteen
rolle's theorem needs the two end values equal
f(1) and f(3) are the same, that is the first equation
rendu chivara values samaanam, so f one equals f three rasta
equate the values at one and at three

steps.why: The question runs the theorem backwards: it gives the conclusion and asks for the function. So both parts of the statement become usable equations, and the equal-end-value part is the cheaper of the two to write.
common_mistakes: Trying to prove f(1) = f(3) instead of using it as given.
Expanding f(3) as 27 + 3b + 3a and losing the 9 in 9b.

steps.label: Use f′(c) = 0 and solve
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Substitute a from (1) BEFORE simplifying — the 4b terms then cancel and only the √3 part is left, which gives b in one line.
steps.memory_tip: A surd left standing on its own must have coefficient zero. That is what determines b here.

recall.must_convey: That f′(c) = 0 at the given c, together with equation (1), gives b = −6 and a = 11.
accept: f dash of c is zero at the given c so b is minus six and a is eleven
substitute a from the first equation and the root three part gives b
differentiate, put the given c in, and solve the two equations
a equals eleven and b equals minus six
f dash c zero pettina, b minus six vasthundi
solve both equations together for a and b

steps.why: This is the second mark because it is the only step that uses the value of c that was given. Check the answer by putting it back: f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 11x has f(1) = f(3) = 6, and f′(x) = 3x² − 12x + 11 is zero at x = 2 ± 1/√3.
common_mistakes: Squaring c wrongly and getting 3c² = 13 + 2√3 instead of 13 + 4√3.
Solving f′(c) = 0 on its own, which is one equation in two unknowns.
